summary: The Upstairs Neighbor asks Bjorn to hold one panel of a flat-pack shelf, and he manages not to turn her small furniture problem into a larger cause.
settingText: Fifth-floor apartment hallway and the Upstairs Neighbor's doorway.

panelPlan.location: fifth-floor hallway outside Upstairs Neighbor's door
panelPlan.action: The Upstairs Neighbor struggles to keep one flat-pack shelving side upright while starting a screw. An open cardboard box partly blocks her doorway.
Bjorn emerges from 5B and looks from the loose upright panel to the scattered hardware and open box, then briefly up and down the hallway.
The neighbor answers without looking up from the hardware.
She puts the loose side panel into Bjorn's hands and points exactly where she wants it held.
Bjorn holds the panel perfectly vertical with both hands fixed in place while the neighbor tightens the hardware herself.

dialogueInline.text: Hold this. Don't improve it. Just hold it.

summary: Carrie arrives to escort Bjorn to the next meeting and learns he already left alone because Gunnar showed him the route once.
settingText: Apartment doorway, Safe Cave interior and a brief view of the block outside.

panelPlan.action: Carrie knocks once and enters with her coat still on, one hand already gesturing back toward the hallway as she calls for Bjorn.

Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin tightens a strap on a household bag. Bjorn, Astrid and Second Male Kin are absent; after Carrie calls, neither Gunnar nor First Male Kin looks toward the door.
Carrie scans the empty window and sleeping side of the studio where Bjorn would normally be, then looks back to Gunnar.
Carrie points her thumb toward the hallway as she asks whether Bjorn left alone. Gunnar turns one page before replying.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick sidewalk half a block from apartment
panelPlan.action: Bjorn walks alone half a block from the apartment through ordinary pedestrian traffic, coat closed and pace steady toward the community center.

dialogueInline.text: Bjorn. Group. We need to leave in five.

summary: When the 1987 Participant asks whether to attend a family dinner that keeps turning them into a period exhibit, Bjorn stops before deciding for them and asks what they actually want.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during a later support-group meeting.

panelPlan.action: 1987 Participant leans forward with hands clasped tightly while describing the invitation. Group Facilitator remains seated elsewhere in the circle, hands resting on their knees.
Bjorn leans forward and starts to give an immediate answer.
Bjorn stops mid-sentence and glances once toward the facilitator. The facilitator keeps their eyes on the participant and their hands still.
Bjorn opens both hands, looks directly at the participant, asks what they want from the dinner, and waits for the answer.
The participant looks down at clasped hands for one beat before answering. As they speak, Bjorn raises one finger at “brother” and a second at “entertainment.”

dialogueInline.text: My brother wants me at dinner. His kids want to meet me. Last time everyone asked what music I remember and whether I knew Reagan.
What do you want from the dinner?
I want to see my brother. I don't want to be the entertainment.

summary: Bjorn gives the 1987 Participant a boundary and an exit rather than deciding whether they should attend the dinner.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room, continuous with Page 15.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn taps two separate points on the edge of the folding coffee table with two fingers as he speaks.
The participant asks what to do when the family starts treating them as entertainment again.
Bjorn points once toward the participant, then holds one flat palm outward while giving the boundary.
Bjorn keeps the flat palm raised through the first sentence, then points toward the room’s exit as he says “leave.”
After his final line, Bjorn lowers both hands to his knees and leans back into his chair.

dialogueInline.text: Go because you want your brother.
And when they start asking me to perform the eighties?
Tell him before you arrive what you will not do.
If he does not defend that boundary in his own hall, leave.
It is a door. You decide whether to use it.

summary: After the meeting, Bjorn and the facilitator agree that adults need ways to contribute and clash over whether contribution should ever become the price of care.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during cleanup, then hallway.

panelPlan.action: Participants stack cups and chairs. Bjorn folds one chair and adds it to the same stack while two other participants clean nearby.
Bjorn and the facilitator continue their argument while carrying chairs toward the wall.
The facilitator keeps carrying a folded chair toward the wall while answering Bjorn.
Bjorn stops his folded chair against the wall and turns to face the facilitator. The facilitator sets their own chair beside it while answering him.
They walk in opposite directions down the hallway, both still wearing tight, irritated expressions.

dialogueInline.text: A person without useful work rots.
If everyone feeds a man and asks nothing of him, they make him a child.
Then ask something of him. Don't make him earn the right to be fed.
You keep coming back for it.

summary: Carrie vents about a DTI deadline mess, and Bjorn asks whether she wants counsel or only a witness before offering any solution.
settingText: Neighborhood coffee cart and nearby sidewalk bench in late afternoon.

panelPlan.action: Carrie walks beside Bjorn with coffee and a folder tucked under one arm, already mid-rant.
Bjorn walks beside Carrie with brows knit, eyes fixed on her and both hands empty and still while she continues.
Bjorn raises one hand slightly and asks his question before Carrie reaches the next complaint.
Carrie stops for half a step and turns to look directly at Bjorn. He meets her eye and repeats the question.

panelPlan.location: sidewalk walking away from coffee cart
panelPlan.action: They resume walking. Carrie says “Witness.” Bjorn delivers one sentence, then goes silent while she answers “Thank you.”

dialogueInline.text: He changed the deadline, then emailed me the old deadline, then asked why I was confused.
And now I have to explain to a man with three calendars how dates work.
Do you want counsel, or witness?
